In the patch 78c52d9eb6b7 (""btrfs: check for refs on snapshot delete
resume"") I added some code to handle file systems that had been
corrupted by a bug that incorrectly skipped updating the drop progress
key while dropping a snapshot.  This code would check to see if we had
already deleted our reference for a child block
if we had already.
Unfortunately there is a bug
column2: as the check would only check the on-disk

column1: references.  I made an incorrect assumption that blocks in an already
deleted snapshot that was having the deletion resume on mount wouldn't
be modified.
If we have 2 pending deleted snapshots that share blocks
modify the rules for a block.  Take the following example
subvolume a exists
column2: and subvolume b is a snapshot of subvolume a.  They

column1: share references to block 1.  Block 1 will have 2 full references
for subvolume a and one for subvolume b
column2: and it belongs to subvolume a

column1: (btrfs_header_owner(block 1) == subvolume a).
When deleting subvolume a
column2: we will drop our full reference for block 1

column1: and because we are the owner we will drop our full reference for all of
block 1's children
reference to all of block 1's children.
Then we will start the snapshot deletion of subvolume b.  We look up the
extent info for block 1
column2: which checks delayed refs and tells us that

column1: FULL BACKREF is set
column2: so sets parent to the bytenr of block 1.  However

column1: because this is a resumed snapshot deletion
check_ref_exists().  Because check_ref_exists() only looks at the disk
it doesn't find the shared backref for the child of block 1
returns 0 and we skip deleting the reference for the child of block 1
and continue.  This orphans the child of block 1.
The fix is to lookup the delayed refs
column2: similar to what we do in

column1: btrfs_lookup_extent_info().  However we only care about whether the
reference exists or not.  If we fail to find our reference on disk
look up the bytenr in the delayed refs
column2: and if it exists look for an

column1: existing ref in the delayed ref head.  If that exists then we know we
can delete the reference safely and carry on.  If it doesn't exist we
know we have to skip over this block.
This bug has existed since I introduced this fix
having multiple deleted snapshots pending when we unmount.  We noticed
this in production because our shutdown path stops the container on the
system
column2: which deletes a bunch of subvolumes

column1: This gives us plenty of opportunities to hit this issue.  Looking at the
history we've seen this occasionally in production
spike recently thanks to faster machines getting jobs with multiple
subvolumes in the job.
Chris Mason wrote a reproducer which does the following
mount /dev/nvme4n1 /btrfs
btrfs subvol create /btrfs/s1
simoop -E -f 4k -n 200000 -z /btrfs/s1
while(true) ; do
btrfs subvol snap /btrfs/s1 /btrfs/s2
simoop -f 4k -n 200000 -r 10 -z /btrfs/s2
btrfs subvol snap /btrfs/s2 /btrfs/s3
btrfs balance start -dusage=80 /btrfs
btrfs subvol del /btrfs/s2 /btrfs/s3
umount /btrfs
btrfsck /dev/nvme4n1 || exit 1
mount /dev/nvme4n1 /btrfs
done
On the second loop this would fail consistently
been running for hours and hasn't failed.
I also used dm-log-writes to capture the state of the failure so I could
debug the problem.  Using the existing failure case to test my patch
validated that it fixes the problem.
